💡 The novelty lies in coupling glycerol-mediated hydrogen-bond regulation with sulfonate outer-sphere interactions to simultaneously tune water states, Zn²⁺ solvation, and ion transport in a hydrogel electrolyte. This multiscale molecular-ionic coupling enables high conductivity (27.3 mS cm⁻¹), suppresses side reactions, and delivers ultrastable Zn anodes (2000 h) and long-cycle full cells, offering a practical electrolyte-engineering strategy for durable aqueous Zn-ion batteries.

💡 The novelty lies in fused-salt-etched nitrogen-modulated fluoride electrolyte (LAFN) using modulus-mismatch-induced interfacial defects between K(Na)Cl and LAFN to create continuous fast Li+ pathways, plus nitrogen doping that forms a stable Li3N-LiF layer and enriches lithium vacancies. Advanced Functional Materials | 🔬 Research Article
💡 Ion-exchange doping of FePS3 with Li+ breaks symmetry, moderately shifting the S p-band center to optimize LiO2/Li2O2 adsorption without passivation. This yields a low 1.53 V overpotential, 11287 mAh g−1 capacity, and stable cycling in Li-O2 batteries. The work establishes ion-mediated symmetry breaking as a strategy for tuning anion-site reactivity in oxygen electrocatalysis.

Journal of the American Chemical Society | 🔬 Research Article
💡 The novelty lies in a multiphase inorganic-rich SEI (Li3P, LiAl5O8, Li3PO4, Li2Al) formed in situ from an ADP interlayer, enabling an integrated Li+ capture-transport mechanism via high affinity, facile desolvation, and low-barrier migration. 💡 The novelty lies in using unconventional Li6MnO4 and MnF2 precursors to reshape the solid-state reaction pathway, suppressing less reactive intermediates and enabling bulk fluorination of Mn-rich DRX cathodes at lower temperature.
